a virtual server → routes for its names on its listeners
→ listener `web`
→ the routes' host matchers (exact names; wildcards of any depth as `HostRegexp`)
prefix → `PathPrefix`, the longest first, below the regular expressions
`Host` is the backend's address (NGINX's default `$proxy_host`); the request URI is passed as it is; the backend's certificate is verified (NGINX's default is not to)

ReverseDock sends the server name (SNI) to TLS backends
prefix → `PathPrefix`, the longest first, below the regular expressions
`Host` is the backend's address (NGINX's default `$proxy_host`); the request URI is passed as it is; the backend's certificate is verified (NGINX's default is not to)
kept on: ReverseDock verifies backend certificates (opt out per service with `tls.verify: false`)
NGINX's default request body limit (`client_max_body_size 1m`) is written as `max_body: 1MiB` on each route (ReverseDock has no limit by default)
NGINX buffers requests and responses by default (`proxy_buffering on`, `proxy_request_buffering on`), which protects backends from slow clients; ReverseDock streams both
NGINX's default connect timeout (`proxy_connect_timeout 60s`) is written as `timeouts.connect: 1m` on each proxied route (ReverseDock's default is 5s)

NGINX rewrites `Location` and `Refresh` headers of backend redirects that point at the `proxy_pass` address (`proxy_redirect default`); ReverseDock passes them unchanged, so a backend that redirects to its own address must use relative or public URLs

requests for hosts no `server_name` lists go to the default server of their listener in NGINX; the migrated routes keep the default server's names, so ReverseDock answers such requests with 404 (add a catch-all route if they mattered)

findings.hint: name the backend's CA (`tls.ca_file`), or set `tls.verify: false` on the service for a self-signed backend you accept
findings.message: NGINX does not verify backend certificates by default (`proxy_ssl_verify off`) and sends no server name (`proxy_ssl_server_name off`); ReverseDock verifies them and sends the name, and the migration keeps that
